cards.text: Someone in the crowd calls out to Jesus, "Teacher," and he's got a request about his brother. Friend, when a man brings up his brother in front of a whole crowd, you KNOW the family group chat is about to go silent for a YEAR.

cards.question: The man in the crowd wants Jesus to tell his brother something. What is it?

answers.text: Pay back what you borrowed from me
Let me move back into the house

cards.question: True or false: Jesus agrees to settle the inheritance between the man and his brother.

cards.text: Jesus answers him, "Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?" Then He says to them, "Watch out!"

cards.question: Jesus warns them to guard themselves against every form of ___.
Jesus gives a reason to guard against greed. What is it?

answers.text: Life is not about how much you own
Riches can be stolen in a moment
Money always splits up a family

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them a parable about a certain rich man whose ground produces an abundance. Not a little extra, friend, AN ABUNDANCE.

cards.question: With a harvest that big, the rich man has nowhere to ___ his crops.

cards.text: So he thinks it over and lands on a plan. I respect a man with a plan, because in the junk drawer my big plan was counting the dust as it fell.

cards.question: The rich man decides what to do about all that grain. What's his plan?

answers.text: Tear down his barns and build bigger ones
Sell all of it before it can spoil
Give the extra away to his neighbors

cards.text: Bigger barns, with all his grain and his goods stored inside. Then he's got a little speech ready, and the only one listening is himself.

cards.question: True or false: The rich man plans to tell himself he has plenty laid up for many years, so he can take it easy.

cards.text: "Eat, drink, and be merry!" This man just put his whole life on Do Not Disturb, but God said to him...

cards.question: God tells the rich man what will happen this very night. What is it?

answers.text: His life will be required of him
His barns will be burned with fire
His grain will be taken by thieves

cards.text: God says to him, "You fool!" He planned for many years and God says this very night, like a man who bought a ten-year planner and only needed one page.

cards.question: True or false: God asks the rich man who will own everything he has accumulated.

cards.text: Then Jesus says this isn't just about one rich man and his barns. It's about anyone who stores up treasure for himself and leaves one thing out.

cards.question: Jesus says it'll be the same for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but isn't rich toward ___.

cards.text: And that's not the end of the teaching, friend. Keep that apron on, because there's more coming.

findings.problem: This true or false card asks whether Jesus agrees to settle the inheritance, but no story card has told any of Jesus's reply yet. The only setup is card 1, so the baker is left with a 50/50 guess. Card 4 then tells the reply right after. The setup should come before the choice: tell enough of Jesus's response first, or ask a question the earlier cards let the baker reason out.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The only humor on this card is restating the text louder: "Not a little extra, friend, AN ABUNDANCE." It reads as emphasis, not a laugh. The moment of a bumper harvest could hold a real joke and should be pushed further.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: "This man just put his whole life on Do Not Disturb" treats the rich man's plan as already done. In Luke 12:19 it is still future ("Then I will say to myself"), and God speaks in 12:20 before any of it happens. Card 11's "Bigger barns, with all his grain and his goods stored inside" can be read the same way. The joke should keep the plan as a plan, for example "is about to put" or "is ready to put."

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This last story card is only the line saying the teaching isn't over, which the docs allow when the last verse was asked on a choice card. It tells no verse, but it cites Luke 12:21, the verse card 18 already covers.
findings.question: What should a story card cite when it holds only the line saying the story isn't over and tells no verses? Should it repeat the passage's last verse, cite nothing, or something else? prep-walkthrough.md says every story card cites exactly the verses it tells, but it doesn't address a card that tells none.
